binders: n is an arbitrary natural number, and the labeled vertex set is Fin n.
p is an arbitrary real number equipped with a proof that 0 <= p <= 1.
E and T are arbitrary finite sets of unordered pairs of vertices from Fin n.
hE proves that every pair in E is non-diagonal, and hT proves that T is a subset of E.
hypotheses: E contains no diagonal unordered pair, so all tested pairs join two distinct vertices.
T is a subset of E.
conclusions: Under the binomial random simple-graph measure on Fin n with parameter p, the set of graphs whose edge set agrees with T on every pair in E has measure p raised to |T| times (1-p) raised to |E|-|T|.
mathematical_definitions: Let V = Fin n and let mu_(n,p) be the measure SimpleGraph.binomialRandom V p, obtained from a set-Bernoulli measure on the non-diagonal unordered pairs through the edge-set representation of simple graphs.
Define C(E,T) = {G : SimpleGraph V | for every e in E, e is an edge of G if and only if e is in T}.
The real unit-interval parameter p and its complement 1-p are converted to nonnegative reals and then embedded into ENNReal; the equality of masses is an equality in ENNReal.
Because T is a subset of E, |E|-|T| is the ordinary nonnegative cardinality difference, even though it is implemented by natural-number subtraction.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every natural number n, every probability parameter p in the closed interval [0,1], every finite loop-free set E of unordered pairs of the n labeled vertices, and every subset T of E, the binomial random graph law with parameter p assigns probability p^{|T|}(1-p)^{|E|-|T|} to the event that, among the pairs tested by E, precisely the pairs in T are edges. The graph's edges outside E are unrestricted.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The vertex set is specifically the finite labeled type Fin n; the claim includes degenerate sizes such as n = 0.
The tested collection E must contain only non-diagonal unordered pairs, and T must be a subset of E; it does not address illegal loop pairs or patterns with required present pairs outside E.
The event constrains adjacency only on E. It imposes no condition on non-diagonal pairs outside E, so it is not the event that the whole graph has edge set T unless E contains every possible edge.
When E is empty, hT forces T to be empty and the event condition is vacuous; the formula becomes 1 using the natural-power convention x^0 = 1, including 0^0 = 1 in this algebraic sense.
The endpoints p = 0 and p = 1 are included. Zero bases combined with zero exponents therefore use the monoid power convention rather than an analytic limiting convention.
Natural subtraction is truncated in general, but the subset hypothesis ensures |T| <= |E|, so the exponent |E|-|T| has its intended cardinality meaning here.

The proposition gives one exact finite edge-pattern product law. It does not separately state an abstract independence predicate, identical-distribution predicate, normalization theorem, or any claim about the packaged degree statistic.
All random objects are undirected simple graphs: orientation, multiple edges, and loops are outside the encoded model.
ambiguities: The dossier exposes that SimpleGraph.binomialRandom is built using ProbabilityTheory.setBernoulli, but it does not expose the definition of setBernoulli itself. Thus the target's exact cylinder-mass equation is unambiguous, while any broader characterization of that underlying measure beyond the displayed construction and asserted law would require additional semantics.
